title: Find the Index of the Large Integer
statement:
A hidden integer array `nums` holds one value that is strictly larger than everything else, and every other position holds the same value. You cannot read `nums` directly. Instead you get an `ArrayReader` object with two methods:

- `length()` returns the number of elements in `nums`.
- `compareSub(l, r, x, y)`, for indexes with `0 <= l <= r < length()` and `0 <= x <= y < length()`, compares the sum of `nums[l..r]` with the sum of `nums[x..y]` (both ranges inclusive). It returns `1` when the first sum is bigger, `0` when the two sums are equal, and `-1` when the first sum is smaller.

Return the index of the large value. You may call `compareSub` at most 20 times; both methods take O(1) time.

Your function is `getIndex(nums)`, and its argument is the `ArrayReader`, not the array (the TypeScript starter types it as `number[]` only because the signature format has no reader type). Each case is written as `[nums]`; the judge wraps `nums` in the reader and stops a solution that calls `compareSub` more than 20 times or with an invalid range.
constraints: All values of nums are equal except one, which is larger than the rest
compareSub may be called at most 20 times per case
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing elements one pair at a time finds the large value, but needs up to `n / 2` calls, far beyond 20. A single `compareSub` call can weigh many elements at once, like a balance scale. Weigh the first half of the candidates against an equally long second half: the heavier side holds the large value, and if they balance, the one element left out (when the count is odd) must be it. Each call halves the candidates, so about `log2(5 * 10^5) < 19` calls suffice.

## Approach

1. Keep the candidates as the inclusive range `[left, right]`, starting with the whole array.
2. While more than one candidate remains, let `half` be half the range's size (rounded down), and compare `[left, leftEnd]` with the next `half` elements `[leftEnd + 1, rightEnd]`.
3. If the first part is heavier, keep it: `right = leftEnd`.
4. If the second part is heavier, keep it: `left = leftEnd + 1`, `right = rightEnd`.
5. If they balance, the size was odd and the unused last element `right` is the answer.
6. When one candidate remains, return `left`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [7, 7, 7, 7, 10, 7, 7, 7]`. The range is `[0, 7]`, so `half = 4`: indexes 0–3 sum to 28 and 4–7 to 31, so `result = -1` and the range becomes `[4, 7]`. Then `half = 2`: indexes 4–5 sum to 17 and 6–7 to 14, so `result = 1` and the range becomes `[4, 5]`. Finally `half = 1`: `10 > 7`, so `right = 4`, and the loop ends with `left = 4`, the answer, after three calls.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n): every call at least halves the range, so at most 19 calls for 5 * 10^5 elements.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Both compared parts must have the same length; otherwise a longer part of small values can outweigh the large one.
- With an odd count the last element is left out, and a balanced result means it is the answer; do not drop it.
- `length` is a method: call `reader.length()`, and pass inclusive ranges to `compareSub`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left`, `right` | inclusive range of indexes that may hold the large value |
| `half` | length of each of the two compared parts |
| `leftEnd` | last index of the first part |
| `rightEnd` | last index of the second part |
| `result` | `compareSub`'s verdict: `1`, `0` or `-1` |

narration.3: ...and ends at the last one, read through length().
narration.5: Keep weighing while more than one index could hold the large value.
narration.6: Each compared part gets half the candidates, rounded down.
narration.7: The first part runs from left to leftEnd.
narration.8: The second part is the next half elements, ending at rightEnd.
narration.9: Weigh the two equally long parts with one call.
narration.11: ...so the large value is in it: shrink the range to the first part.
narration.13: ...so the range starts right after the first part...
narration.14: ...and ends where the second part ends.
narration.16: The parts balance, so the size was odd and the left-out last index holds the large value.
narration.19: Only one candidate is left: it is the large value's index.
